blockMcqs.question: Which scheme best fits a latency-critical service on a large heap?
options: A concurrent collector like ZGC or Go
blockMcqs.explanation: Concurrent collectors trace alongside the app, holding pauses under a millisecond.

blockMcqs.question: Why is stack allocation faster than heap allocation?
options: The stack lives in CPU registers
Freeing is just popping a single pointer
The heap is encrypted by the runtime
blockMcqs.explanation: A frame is reclaimed by moving one pointer on return, no search needed.

blockMcqs.question: Which bug most often becomes an exploitable security hole?
blockMcqs.explanation: Freed bytes get reused, so an attacker can plant controlled data there.

blockMcqs.question: What can reference counting alone never reclaim?
blockMcqs.explanation: Mutually-referencing objects keep each other's count above zero forever.

blockMcqs.question: Which collector leaves the heap fragmented?
blockMcqs.explanation: It never relocates objects, so dead gaps remain between live ones.

blockMcqs.question: Why does generational GC collect the young gen often?
options: Young objects are larger on average
Most objects die young, so survivors are few
The old gen cannot be scanned at all
blockMcqs.explanation: With most of the region dead, copying the rare survivors is cheap.

blockMcqs.question: Why does the tracer reclaim the a/b cycle the example builds?
options: Nothing reachable points into that island
Cycles are freed before any GC runs
The compiler rewrote the cycle away
blockMcqs.explanation: Reachability ignores internal links; an unrooted island is simply never visited.

blockMcqs.question: How do concurrent collectors shrink stop-the-world pauses?
options: By tracing alongside the app with tri-color marking
By collecting only the old generation
blockMcqs.explanation: A write barrier keeps the snapshot safe while the app keeps mutating pointers.

blockMcqs.question: In one line, what is the central GC tuning trade-off?
blockMcqs.explanation: More heap headroom means rarer collections; less means the GC runs constantly.

blockMcqs.question: Which signal most clearly indicates a memory leak?
options: Old-gen occupancy after major GC climbing steadily
blockMcqs.explanation: Live data that never returns to baseline means objects are wrongly retained.

blockMcqs.question: Can a garbage-collected language still leak memory?
options: Only if reference counting is enabled
Yes, by keeping objects reachable forever
Only on heaps larger than 4 GB
blockMcqs.explanation: An unbounded cache or static collection stays reachable, so GC never frees it.
